stories.title: CBSE releases 2027 board exam schedule
stories.summary: The Central Board of Secondary Education has released its 2027 date sheet for Class 12 board exams. Testing will run from February 16 to April 9, 2027. Papers will commence at 10:30 am. The board says it has provided adequate gaps between subjects commonly taken together.

stories.title: Students petition for third JEE Advanced attempt
stories.summary: Over 13,400 engineering aspirants have signed an online petition urging the IIT Council and Joint Admission Board to permit a third attempt at the JEE Advanced 2027. The campaign seeks parity with JEE Main and relief for second droppers. The race for seats is getting tougher.

stories.summary: The Central Board of Secondary Education will begin Class 10 and 12 board exams on February 16, 2027. Class 10 exams conclude March 9, while Class 12 ends April 9. Examination Controller Sanyam Bhardwaj noted the schedule was released 101 days before the start of the exams.

stories.title: NEET 2027 exam mode remains offline
stories.summary: The NEET UG 2027 exam is expected to remain a pen and paper test. A planned shift to computer based testing may be delayed as the Centre extended the tenure of the examination reform task force led by Nandan Nilekani until January 2027. The panel is still consulting.

stories.title: Arizona universities report drop in international enrollment
stories.summary: Arizona's three public universities report significant declines in international student enrollment, attributing the trend to federal immigration and visa policies. Northern Arizona University saw a 32 percent drop, while Arizona State and the University of Arizona fell 21 percent and 18 percent respectively. It is a national pattern.

stories.title: Iceland eases work rules for international students
stories.summary: Iceland has amended its Act on Foreign Nationals to allow students with valid residence permits to work without separate permits. Students may work up to 60 percent of full-time hours during the academic year. Limits are lifted during official breaks and after graduation while staying in the country.

stories.title: Canada maintains international student arrival targets
stories.summary: Canada will keep its target of 150,000 international student arrivals annually through 2029. The goal is part of a broader plan to welcome 370,000 temporary residents each year. The targets for 2027 and 2028 remain unchanged from the previous immigration plan released last year.

stories.title: Iceland Relaxes Work Permit Rules for International Students
stories.summary: Iceland has announced new rules allowing international students with valid residence permits to work in the country without obtaining a separate work permit. According to the Directorate of Immigration, the changes follow amendments to the Icelandic Act on Foreign Nationals and the Foreign Nationals’ Right

stories.title: Australia offers training visa for foreign nationals
stories.summary: Australia’s Subclass 407 Training Visa allows eligible foreigners to complete workplace-based occupational training for up to two years. The visa costs from AUD 535 for the main applicant. Candidates must secure an approved sponsor and nomination before they are permitted to lodge a visa application.

stories.title: Georgetown MBA applications drop 22 percent
stories.summary: Applications to the Georgetown University McDonough School of Business full-time MBA program fell 22 percent for the Class of 2028. The cohort size shrank from 248 students to 197. The school says the degree continues to attract high-quality applicants while navigating the current environment.

stories.title: Stanford researcher loses visa lawsuit
stories.summary: A Chinese doctoral student at Stanford University sued the federal government after his visa renewal stalled in a State Department review. A federal judge dismissed the case, ruling that courts lack the legal authority to intervene in consular processing. The student remains in limbo.

stories.title: Australia reviews student visa requirements
stories.summary: The Australian government is consulting on reforms to its Genuine Student test and financial requirements. The move follows record numbers of international student visa rejections over the past year. The government aims to discourage visa hopping and the growth of what it terms permanent temporary migrants.

stories.title: US election results and higher education
stories.summary: Democrats have secured control of both chambers of Congress following the midterm elections. The shift occurs as the current administration continues to restrict opportunities for international students. The Presidents Alliance on Higher Education and Immigration says the results show voters are paying attention to fairness.

stories.title: Philippines to fast-track student visas
stories.summary: The Philippines Commission on Higher Education is launching a strategy to streamline student and faculty mobility. Modelled on a system in Malaysia, the initiative aims to make the arrival of international students and academics effortless. The country is attempting to transform into a vibrant destination for talent.

stories.title: Artemis Gold launches Indigenous scholarship
stories.summary: Artemis Gold is funding a scholarship program for up to five Indigenous Grade 12 students annually. The award covers four years of postsecondary education in fields related to the mining industry. The company says the goal is to set students on a path toward mining careers.

stories.title: Bet9ja announces 2027 undergraduate scholarships
stories.summary: The Bet9ja Foundation is offering full tuition support to Nigerian undergraduates in their third or fourth year of study. Applicants must maintain a CGPA of at least 4.0 in STEM, law, medicine, humanities or administration. The foundation says the program aims to improve access to education.

stories.title: Reno Rodeo Foundation opens scholarship applications
stories.summary: The Reno Rodeo Foundation is accepting applications for college degrees, trade certifications and career training programs through February 28, 2027. The foundation awarded $113,500 to 29 students in 2026. It notes that a four-year degree is one of many paths to a successful future.

stories.title: NAPB-APBA Borlaug scholarship for African PhD students
stories.summary: The NAPB Borlaug Scholars Africa Programme is inviting applications from doctoral students in plant breeding and agricultural sciences. The program offers six awards to researchers at African institutions, providing financial support, professional mentorship and international exposure. The scholarship aims to nurture the next generation of plant breeding scientists.

stories.title: Scholarship opportunities for Pakistani students
stories.summary: Universities and governments are offering fully funded scholarships for 2027 covering tuition, stipends and airfare for Pakistani students. Programs in Europe, the UK, Canada, Switzerland and the Middle East provide financial assistance for undergraduate and postgraduate studies. Studying abroad remains a dream often held back by costs.

stories.title: Turkey announces student loan and scholarship results
stories.summary: The Ministry of Youth and Sports has released the results for its 2026 scholarship and education loan applications. Students must approve a commitment form via the e-Devlet portal by November 11. The ministry provides this financial support to students enrolled in higher education institutions.

stories.title: University of Lodz receives funding for international services
stories.summary: The University of Lodz will receive nearly half a million zlotys to enhance services for international students and staff. The funding supports administrative training and international promotion. The university strategy identifies internationalisation as a key pillar of its development through the year 2030.

stories.title: Municipal scholarships available in São Brás de Alportel
stories.summary: University students residing in São Brás de Alportel are now eligible to apply for municipal scholarships. The local government has opened the application process for the current academic year. Further details regarding the program are available through the municipal office.

stories.title: Keio University welcomes international scholars
stories.summary: Keio University hosted a welcome gathering for incoming international scholars and students. The event was organized by the deans of the Faculty of Science and Technology and the Graduate School of Science and Technology. Details of the gathering were posted on the university website.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia offers government-funded scholarships
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia is offering government-funded scholarships to international students to pursue higher education at recognized universities. The program aims to help students avoid the financial burden of studying abroad. The country has been investing significantly in its education sector to attract international talent.

stories.title: Vidyadhan Mathura scholarship for women in STEM
stories.summary: The Vidyadhan Mathura scholarship is offering up to 75,000 INR in annual financial support for women pursuing studies in STEM fields. The application process is currently managed through the program website. The scholarship aims to provide financial assistance to students during their academic journey.

stories.title: Collaboratory opens 2027 scholarship cycle
stories.summary: Collaboratory is accepting scholarship applications for the 2027 academic year until January 14. The program provides financial support to high school seniors, adult learners and students pursuing technical or degree programs. Residents of five Florida counties are eligible to apply for the distributed funds.

stories.title: Chinese universities dominate global chemistry rankings
stories.summary: Chinese universities hold seven of the top 10 spots in the latest global chemistry rankings. Tsinghua University placed first, followed by Stanford University and the University of California, Berkeley. The rankings reflect the research output and academic standing of institutions worldwide.

stories.title: Graphic Era secures 101st rank in South Asia
stories.summary: Graphic Era Deemed University has secured the 101st rank in South Asia and 415th in Asia in the latest QS Asia University Rankings. The institution says it demonstrated excellence across parameters including research quality and academic reputation. It has now strengthened its position in the global rankings.

stories.title: Mount St. Mary's University rises in rankings
stories.summary: Mount St. Mary's University reached No. 64 among regional universities in the 2026-27 U.S. News & World Report rankings, an eight-spot increase. The institution also rose to No. 17 for best value. The university attributes these gains to its commitment to academic excellence and student success.

stories.title: Far Eastern University reports ranking gains
stories.summary: Far Eastern University has maintained its presence in the QS Asia University Rankings. The institution reports significant gains across key performance indicators. The university continues to feature in the regional list.

stories.title: UGM takes top national spot in Indonesia
stories.summary: Universitas Gadjah Mada ranked 53rd in the 2027 QS Asia University Rankings, overtaking Universitas Indonesia. UGM achieved an overall score of 82.2, improving two places from the previous edition. Universitas Airlangga followed in second place nationally, with Universitas Indonesia placing third.

stories.title: KUHeS enters world university rankings
stories.summary: Kamuzu University of Health Sciences is the only Malawian institution in the 2027 Times Higher Education World University Rankings. The university appears in the same list as Harvard and Oxford, though it remains several ranking bands below them. It is currently ranked above its regional neighbours.

stories.title: ICAR institutions debut in global rankings
stories.summary: Two deemed universities under the Indian Council of Agricultural Research have entered the QS World University Rankings by Subject 2026. This maiden entry follows a national priority to develop skilled human capital as emphasized by the Prime Minister. The institutions are working toward a vision of Viksit Bharat.

stories.title: Central Philippine University maintains regional standing
stories.summary: Central Philippine University ranked 22nd in the Philippines and within the 1,301-1,400 bracket in the 2027 QS Asia University Rankings. The institution also placed 205th in Southeast Asia. The rankings evaluated the university on indicators including research, discovery, and global engagement.

stories.title: Macao Polytechnic University climbs regional rankings
stories.summary: Macao Polytechnic University reached 306th in the 2027 QS Asia University Rankings, climbing nearly 100 places. The university recorded improved scores in academic reputation, research publications, and international networks. The institution says the result reflects its continued progress in teaching quality and innovation.

stories.title: Wenzhou-Kean University rises in Asia rankings
stories.summary: Wenzhou-Kean University climbed 229 places to No. 751 in the 2027 QS Asia University Rankings. The institution ranked 178th among universities in the Chinese mainland. Its international faculty ratio earned a full score, ranking first among universities in the region.

stories.title: Shoolini University leads in citations per paper
stories.summary: Shoolini University is joint No. 1 in Asia for citations per paper for the second consecutive year, according to the QS World University Rankings: Asia 2027. The university ranked 177th overall. Its research output per faculty member improved by 90 places from the previous year.

stories.title: Lovely Professional University rises in Asia rankings
stories.summary: Lovely Professional University reached 154th in the 2027 QS Asia University Rankings, rising 33 places. The institution secured the 12th position nationally and 2nd among private universities in India. It claims to have surpassed several IITs and all NITs in the international research network category.

stories.title: Cornell faculty approve no confidence resolution
stories.summary: Cornell University faculty senators voted 55.6 percent in favor of a no confidence resolution against the administration. The vote follows allegations regarding the university's handling of a sexual assault case. About 37 percent of senators voted against the resolution, with 7.4 percent abstaining.

stories.title: Cornell leadership faces no confidence vote
stories.summary: The Cornell University Faculty Senate approved a no confidence resolution against top leaders following a former student's lawsuit alleging a 2024 fraternity gang rape. The resolution passed 75-50. Professors have debated the administration's response to the allegation for several weeks.

stories.title: DOJ sues Penn State over tuition policy
stories.summary: The federal government has filed a lawsuit against Penn State regarding its in-state tuition policies for undocumented students. The agency appears to be targeting individual colleges after previous legal challenges at the state level. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: University of Maine offers faculty buyouts
stories.summary: The University of Maine is offering buyouts to 158 faculty members to address a $19 million structural deficit. University leaders say the move is intended to minimize layoffs. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: UC board reviews standardized testing requirements
stories.summary: The University of California Board of Admissions is meeting to discuss whether to reinstate SAT and ACT scores as an admission requirement. Researchers are evaluating whether testing acts as a solution for improving math readiness. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: College Board addresses AI cheating on SAT
stories.summary: The College Board is implementing new measures to combat AI-assisted cheating on the SAT. The organization is adjusting its testing protocols to maintain exam integrity. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: Student union opposes work authorization fee
stories.summary: The Associated Students of the University of California is calling on the university to oppose a $100,000 international student work authorization fee. The union is seeking to mitigate costs for the student body. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: ANU council approved savings target without discussion
stories.summary: The Australian National University governing council approved a 250 million dollar savings target despite a proposal for 200 million dollars. Minutes show no discussion on how the higher figure was chosen or its impact on operations. The council had four days to consider the final plan.

stories.title: UGC equity rules review status
stories.summary: The full piece is for subscribers. Access to the report regarding the University Grants Commission equity rules review is currently restricted for this user. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: Gannon University global enrollment drops
stories.summary: Gannon University global enrollment has fallen to 430 students, down from nearly 1,000 international students just a few years ago. The university previously ranked fifth among Pennsylvania colleges for international diversity. The decline has forced the school to cut costs.

stories.title: Jharkhand High Court reinstates JSSC-CGL exam results
stories.summary: The Jharkhand High Court quashed the state government decision to cancel the JSSC-CGL exam. Justice Deepak Roshan ordered the reinstatement of candidates selected under advertisement 10/2023, directing that their service be treated as continuous. The government had previously cited a CID report and protests as reasons for cancellation.

stories.title: Government delays decision on UGC rules
stories.summary: The Indian government has extended the decision-making period for contentious University Grants Commission rules following widespread debate. Officials stated no clear stance has been taken, leaving administrators and students waiting for clarity. The UGC was established to enhance the quality of higher education across India.
